subject: maths
title: Time and Measures
bookChapter: No separate book chapter: Stage 6 time objective 6Gt.01, plus measure conversions used throughout the book

preamble.whatYouWillLearn: You will change times between decimals and hours and minutes, like 2.5 hours = 2 hours 30 minutes. You will work out how long things take using the 24-hour clock and timetables, even past midnight. You will convert lengths, masses and capacities, and solve perimeter and area problems with mixed units.
preamble.whyItMatters: Time does not work like ordinary decimals, because an hour has 60 minutes, not 100. Knowing this stops a very common mistake. Changing units correctly is needed in almost every measurement question in your exams.
realWorld: Working out how long a bus from KL to Penang takes using the timetable
Changing a recipe's 1.5 kg of rice into grams for the kitchen scale
Counting how many floor tiles are needed for a room
Knowing a 0.75-hour badminton session is 45 minutes, not 75
Working out what time a night flight lands after crossing midnight

subtopics.title: Time as decimals and mixed units
subtopics.summary: Convert time between decimal hours and hours and minutes, for example 1.75 h = 1 h 45 min and 0.2 h = 12 min.

subtopics.title: Time calculations and timetables
subtopics.summary: Find durations and end times using the 12-hour and 24-hour clock, timetables and times that go past midnight.

subtopics.title: Converting metric units
subtopics.summary: Change between mm, cm, m and km; g and kg; ml and l by multiplying or dividing by 10, 100 or 1000.

subtopics.title: Measurement word problems
subtopics.summary: Solve problems about perimeter, area and distances where the measurements are given in different units.

questions.prompt: How long is 2.5 hours in hours and minutes?
questions.solution: The 2 is 2 whole hours. The 0.5 means half an hour. Half of 60 minutes is 30 minutes. So 2.5 hours = 2 hours 30 minutes.

misconceptions.0: You read the .5 as 50 minutes. But an hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so 0.5 of an hour is half of 60 = 30 minutes.
misconceptions.1: You multiplied 2.5 by 100. There are 60 minutes in an hour, so 2.5 hours = 2.5 x 60 = 150 minutes.
misconceptions.3: You read the digit 5 as 5 minutes. The 5 is 5 tenths of an hour, and 0.5 x 60 = 30 minutes.

questions.skill: converting decimal hours to hours and minutes

questions.prompt: How many minutes are there in 0.75 hours? Give your answer in minutes.
questions.solution: 0.75 is the same as 3/4. One quarter of an hour is 60 / 4 = 15 minutes, so three quarters is 3 x 15 = 45 minutes. Or work it out as 0.75 x 60 = 45.

misconceptions.common: Answering 75 minutes by reading the decimal digits as minutes. An hour has 60 minutes, so multiply by 60: 0.75 x 60 = 45.

questions.prompt: Which shows 1 hour 45 minutes as a decimal number of hours?
questions.solution: 45 minutes is 45 out of 60 minutes, which is 45/60 = 3/4 of an hour. 3/4 = 0.75. So 1 hour 45 minutes = 1.75 hours.

misconceptions.0: You copied the 45 minutes straight after the decimal point. Minutes are sixtieths of an hour, not hundredths, so 45 minutes = 45/60 = 0.75 h.
misconceptions.2: 0.25 h is only a quarter of an hour, which is 15 minutes. 45 minutes is three quarters of an hour, so it is 0.75 h.
misconceptions.3: 1 hour 45 minutes is 105 MINUTES, not 105 hours. To change minutes to hours, divide by 60: 105 / 60 = 1.75 h.

questions.skill: converting hours and minutes to decimal hours

questions.prompt: How many minutes is 0.2 hours?
questions.solution: 0.2 hours means 2 tenths of an hour. One tenth of 60 minutes is 6 minutes, so 2 tenths is 2 x 6 = 12 minutes. Or: 0.2 x 60 = 12.

misconceptions.1: You read 0.2 as 20 minutes, as if an hour had 100 minutes. An hour has 60 minutes, so 0.2 x 60 = 12 minutes.
misconceptions.2: You read the digit 2 as 2 minutes. The 2 means 2 tenths of an hour, and one tenth of an hour is 6 minutes.
misconceptions.3: You worked out 2 x 60 and lost the decimal point. 0.2 is much less than 1 hour, so the answer must be less than 60 minutes.

questions.prompt: True or false: 3.3 hours is the same as 3 hours 30 minutes.
questions.solution: 0.3 hours is 3 tenths of an hour. One tenth of an hour is 6 minutes, so 0.3 h = 3 x 6 = 18 minutes. So 3.3 hours = 3 hours 18 minutes, not 3 hours 30 minutes. The statement is false.

misconceptions.common: Reading the digits after the decimal point as minutes. Hours are split into 60 minutes, not 100, so 0.3 h = 0.3 x 60 = 18 minutes. (3 hours 30 minutes would be 3.5 hours.)

questions.skill: converting decimal hours to hours and minutes

questions.prompt: Write 4.25 hours in hours and minutes.
questions.solution: 4 whole hours stay as 4 hours. 0.25 = 1/4, and a quarter of 60 minutes is 15 minutes. So 4.25 hours = 4 hours 15 minutes.

misconceptions.common: Writing 4 hours 25 minutes. The .25 is a quarter of an hour, which is 15 minutes, because an hour has 60 minutes, not 100.

questions.skill: converting decimal hours to hours and minutes

questions.prompt: Write 2 hours 24 minutes as a decimal number of hours. Give your answer as a decimal.
questions.solution: Change the minutes to a fraction of an hour: 24/60. Divide top and bottom by 12 to get 2/5. 2/5 = 0.4. So 2 hours 24 minutes = 2.4 hours.

misconceptions.common: Writing 2.24 hours by putting the minutes after the decimal point. Minutes are sixtieths of an hour, so 24 minutes = 24/60 = 0.4 h.

questions.skill: converting hours and minutes to decimal hours

questions.prompt: A film lasts 96 minutes. How long is that as a decimal number of hours?
questions.solution: Divide by 60 to change minutes to hours: 96 / 60 = 1.6. Check: 1.6 h = 1 hour + 0.6 x 60 minutes = 1 hour 36 minutes = 96 minutes.

misconceptions.0: 96 minutes is 1 hour 36 minutes, but 36 minutes is not 0.36 h. 36 minutes = 36/60 = 0.6 h, so the answer is 1.6 h.
misconceptions.1: You divided by 100 as if an hour had 100 minutes. Divide by 60: 96 / 60 = 1.6 h. (96 minutes is more than 1 hour, so the answer must be more than 1.)
misconceptions.2: You divided by 10 instead of 60. 9.6 hours would be almost 10 hours, far too long for a film of 96 minutes.

questions.prompt: Match each time in decimal hours to the same time in hours and minutes.
questions.solution: Multiply the decimal part by 60. 0.5 x 60 = 30, so 1.5 h = 1 h 30 min. 0.1 x 60 = 6, so 1.1 h = 1 h 6 min. 0.25 x 60 = 15, so 1.25 h = 1 h 15 min. 0.9 x 60 = 54, so 1.9 h = 1 h 54 min.

misconceptions.common: Copying the decimal digits as minutes, for example matching 1.1 h with 1 h 10 min or 1.5 h with 1 h 50 min. Multiply the decimal part by 60 instead.

questions.skill: converting decimal hours to hours and minutes

questions.prompt: Put these lengths of time in order from shortest to longest.
questions.solution: Change them all to minutes. 1.2 hours = 1.2 x 60 = 72 minutes. 75 minutes stays 75. 1.3 hours = 1.3 x 60 = 78 minutes. 1 hour 20 minutes = 60 + 20 = 80 minutes. Shortest to longest: 1.2 hours, 75 minutes, 1.3 hours, 1 hour 20 minutes.

misconceptions.common: Thinking 1.3 hours is 1 hour 30 minutes and putting it last. 0.3 h is only 0.3 x 60 = 18 minutes, so 1.3 hours = 78 minutes.

questions.prompt: Aisha practised the piano for 0.4 hours on Monday and for 1 hour 35 minutes on Tuesday. How long did she practise altogether?
questions.solution: First change 0.4 hours to minutes: 0.4 x 60 = 24 minutes. Then add: 24 minutes + 1 hour 35 minutes = 1 hour 59 minutes. Well done if you changed to the same units first!

misconceptions.0: You took 0.4 hours to be 40 minutes. An hour has 60 minutes, so 0.4 h = 0.4 x 60 = 24 minutes, not 40.
misconceptions.2: You added 0.4 + 1.35, treating 1 hour 35 minutes as 1.35 hours. 35 minutes is not 0.35 h. Change both to minutes before adding.
misconceptions.3: You took 0.4 hours to be 4 minutes. 0.4 is 4 tenths of an hour, and each tenth is 6 minutes, so 0.4 h = 24 minutes.

questions.skill: adding times given in different forms

questions.prompt: Select ALL the lengths of time that are LONGER than 2.4 hours.
questions.solution: Change everything to minutes. 2.4 hours = 2 x 60 + 0.4 x 60 = 120 + 24 = 144 minutes. 2 h 30 min = 150 (longer). 2 h 20 min = 140 (shorter). 145 minutes (longer). 2.35 hours = 120 + 0.35 x 60 = 120 + 21 = 141 (shorter). 2 h 25 min = 145 (longer).

misconceptions.1: 2 h 20 min = 140 minutes, which is less than 2.4 h = 144 minutes.
misconceptions.3: 2.35 hours = 141 minutes, which is less than 144 minutes. Compare 2.35 and 2.40 as decimals: 2.35 is smaller.
misconceptions.common: Thinking 2.4 hours means 2 hours 40 minutes (160 minutes). Then nothing on the list would look longer. 0.4 h is 24 minutes, so 2.4 h = 2 h 24 min.

questions.prompt: What is 7:45 pm written in the 24-hour clock?
questions.solution: For times after midday (pm), add 12 to the hour. 7 + 12 = 19. So 7:45 pm = 19:45.

misconceptions.0: 07:45 is 7:45 in the MORNING (am). For pm times you add 12 to the hour.
misconceptions.1: A common mix-up: 17:45 looks like it has a 7, but 17:45 is 5:45 pm. Add 12, not 10: 7 + 12 = 19.

questions.prompt: A lesson starts at 09:20 and ends at 10:05. How long is the lesson? Give your answer in minutes.
questions.solution: Count on. From 09:20 to 10:00 is 40 minutes. From 10:00 to 10:05 is 5 minutes. 40 + 5 = 45 minutes.

misconceptions.common: Taking away the times like ordinary numbers: 1005 - 920 = 85. Times do not work like that because an hour has 60 minutes, not 100. Count on to the next hour instead.

questions.prompt: A bus leaves at 14:35 and arrives at 17:10. How long is the journey? Give your answer in hours and minutes.
questions.solution: Count on. 14:35 to 16:35 is 2 hours. 16:35 to 17:00 is 25 minutes. 17:00 to 17:10 is 10 minutes. 2 hours + 25 minutes + 10 minutes = 2 hours 35 minutes.

misconceptions.common: Subtracting like ordinary numbers (1710 - 1435 = 275) and writing 2 hours 75 minutes. A time cannot have 75 minutes; count on through the hour instead.

questions.prompt: A night flight leaves Kuala Lumpur at 22:50. It lands 6 hours 25 minutes later. Both times are Kuala Lumpur time. What time does it land?
questions.solution: Add the hours first: 22:50 + 6 hours = 28:50. A day only has 24 hours, so take away 24: 28:50 is 04:50 the next morning. Now add 25 minutes: 04:50 + 10 minutes = 05:00, then 15 more minutes = 05:15.

misconceptions.0: You added correctly but forgot that the clock starts again at 00:00 after midnight. Take away 24 hours: 29:15 - 24:00 = 05:15.
misconceptions.1: 50 + 25 = 75 minutes, which is 1 hour 15 minutes. You wrote the 15 but forgot to carry the extra hour.
misconceptions.3: You subtracted 6 h 25 min instead of adding. The plane lands AFTER it leaves, so the time must be later.

questions.prompt: Wei Ming falls asleep at 22:40 and wakes up at 06:15 the next morning. How long does he sleep?
questions.solution: Count on in steps. 22:40 to 23:00 is 20 minutes. 23:00 to 06:00 is 7 hours. 06:00 to 06:15 is 15 minutes. 7 hours + 20 minutes + 15 minutes = 7 hours 35 minutes.

misconceptions.1: You worked out 22:40 - 06:15, which is the time from 06:15 to 22:40, when he is awake. He sleeps from 22:40 through midnight to 06:15, so count on from 22:40.
misconceptions.2: You took away the hours (30 - 22 = 8) and the minutes (40 - 15 = 25) separately. The minutes go the wrong way, so you must count on through the hour.
misconceptions.3: You counted 22:40 to 23:00 (20 minutes) and 23:00 to 06:00 (7 hours) but forgot the last 15 minutes from 06:00 to 06:15.

questions.prompt: Part of a bus timetable shows: Ipoh 07:40, Tapah 08:25, Rawang 09:50, Kuala Lumpur 10:15. How long does the bus take from Tapah to Kuala Lumpur?
questions.solution: Tapah is 08:25 and Kuala Lumpur is 10:15. Count on: 08:25 to 09:25 is 1 hour. 09:25 to 10:00 is 35 minutes. 10:00 to 10:15 is 15 minutes. 1 hour + 35 + 15 minutes = 1 hour 50 minutes.

misconceptions.0: That is the time from Ipoh (07:40), the first stop. The question starts at Tapah (08:25). Read the timetable carefully.
misconceptions.1: You subtracted 1015 - 825 = 190 like ordinary numbers. An hour has 60 minutes, so '90 minutes' is not possible here. Count on instead.
misconceptions.2: You took away the hours (10 - 8 = 2) and then took 15 from 25 the wrong way round. Count on through the hour instead.

questions.prompt: True or false: 00:30 on the 24-hour clock is half an hour after midnight.
questions.solution: On the 24-hour clock, midnight is 00:00. So 00:30 is 30 minutes after midnight, which is 12:30 am. The statement is true.

misconceptions.common: Thinking 00:30 is 12:30 in the afternoon. Half past twelve in the afternoon is 12:30 on the 24-hour clock; 00:30 is just after midnight.

questions.prompt: These times are all on the same day. Put them in order from earliest to latest.
questions.solution: Change them all to the 24-hour clock: 2:15 pm = 14:15, 09:40, 11:30 am = 11:30, 00:45, 18:05. Earliest to latest: 00:45, 09:40, 11:30 am, 2:15 pm, 18:05.

misconceptions.common: Putting 2:15 pm early because 2 is a small number. pm means after midday, so 2:15 pm is 14:15. Also, 00:45 is just after midnight, so it is the earliest.

questions.prompt: A cooking class has 3 sessions. Each session lasts 1 hour 40 minutes. There is a 15-minute break between sessions (2 breaks in total). The class starts at 09:30. At what time does it finish? Use the 24-hour clock.
questions.solution: Sessions: 3 x 1 h 40 min = 3 h 120 min = 5 hours. Breaks: 2 x 15 min = 30 minutes. Total time = 5 hours 30 minutes. 09:30 + 5 hours = 14:30. 14:30 + 30 minutes = 15:00.

misconceptions.common: Counting 3 breaks instead of 2. With 3 sessions there are only 2 gaps between them. Another slip is writing 3 x 1 h 40 min as 3 h 40 min; remember to multiply the minutes too.

questions.prompt: A ferry leaves at 21:35 on Friday. The trip takes 9 hours 50 minutes. When does the ferry arrive?
questions.solution: 21:35 + 9 hours = 30:35. That is past midnight, so take away 24 hours: 06:35 on Saturday. Now add 50 minutes: 06:35 + 25 minutes = 07:00, then 25 more minutes = 07:25. The ferry arrives at 07:25 on Saturday.

misconceptions.0: The time is right, but the ferry travels through midnight, so it arrives the next day, Saturday.
misconceptions.1: 35 + 50 = 85 minutes, which is 1 hour 25 minutes. You wrote 25 but forgot to carry the extra hour.
misconceptions.2: The 24-hour clock only goes up to 23:59. After midnight it starts again at 00:00 on the next day: 31:25 - 24:00 = 07:25 on Saturday.

questions.prompt: A movie marathon starts at 19:45 and ends at 01:20 the next morning. How long does it last? Give your answer in minutes.
questions.solution: 19:45 to 20:00 is 15 minutes. 20:00 to midnight (24:00) is 4 hours = 240 minutes. Midnight to 01:20 is 80 minutes. Total = 15 + 240 + 80 = 335 minutes (that is 5 hours 35 minutes).

misconceptions.common: Doing 19:45 - 01:20 and getting 18 h 25 min. The marathon goes past midnight, so count on from 19:45 to midnight, then from midnight to 01:20.

questions.prompt: What is 16:20 written in the 12-hour clock?
questions.solution: Hours bigger than 12 are in the afternoon or evening. Take away 12: 16 - 12 = 4. So 16:20 is 4:20 pm.

misconceptions.1: You took away 10 instead of 12 (16 - 10 = 6). Always take away 12 to change a pm time back to the 12-hour clock.
misconceptions.2: 4:20 am is early morning, which is 04:20. Any hour of 13 or more is after midday, so it is pm.

questions.prompt: How many grams are there in 3.5 kg?

misconceptions.0: You multiplied by 100. There are 1000 grams in 1 kilogram, so multiply by 1000.
misconceptions.1: You multiplied by 10. There are 1000 grams in 1 kilogram, so multiply by 1000.
misconceptions.2: You read 3.5 kg as 3 kg and 5 g. The 5 is 5 tenths of a kilogram, which is 500 g, so 3.5 kg = 3 kg 500 g = 3500 g.

questions.prompt: How many centimetres are there in 2.4 m?
questions.solution: 1 m = 100 cm, so multiply by 100. 2.4 x 100 = 240. So 2.4 m = 240 cm.

misconceptions.0: You multiplied by 10. There are 100 cm in 1 m, so multiply by 100.
misconceptions.2: You multiplied by 1000. That is the rule for metres to millimetres. There are 100 cm in 1 m.
misconceptions.3: You divided by 100 instead of multiplying. Centimetres are smaller than metres, so you need MORE of them: the number gets bigger.

questions.prompt: Write 750 ml in litres. Give your answer as a decimal.

misconceptions.common: Dividing by 100 and getting 7.5 L. There are 1000 ml in a litre, so divide by 1000. (A 750 ml bottle is less than 1 litre, so 7.5 L cannot be right.)

questions.prompt: Write 4 km 60 m in kilometres.

misconceptions.1: 4.6 km would be 4 km 600 m. 60 m is 60 thousandths of a km, so it is 0.060 km, not 0.6 km. Use a zero to hold the tenths place.
misconceptions.3: 4 km 60 m is 4060 METRES. In kilometres it is 4060 / 1000 = 4.06 km.

questions.prompt: True or false: 1 litre is the same as 1000 millilitres.
questions.solution: Milli means one thousandth. 1 millilitre is 1/1000 of a litre, so 1000 millilitres make 1 litre. The statement is true.

misconceptions.common: Thinking 1 litre = 100 ml, mixing it up with 1 m = 100 cm. For litres and millilitres the number is 1000.

questions.prompt: Fill in the missing unit: 5 cm = 50 ___
questions.solution: 1 cm = 10 mm. So 5 cm = 5 x 10 = 50 mm. The missing unit is millimetres (mm).

misconceptions.common: Writing m (metres). 50 m is a whole running track, much longer than 5 cm. The unit must be smaller than a centimetre: millimetres.

questions.prompt: Put these masses in order from lightest to heaviest.
questions.solution: Change them all to grams. 1.2 kg = 1200 g, 950 g, 1 kg 25 g = 1025 g, 1050 g, 0.9 kg = 900 g. Lightest to heaviest: 0.9 kg (900 g), 950 g, 1 kg 25 g (1025 g), 1050 g, 1.2 kg (1200 g).

misconceptions.common: Comparing the numbers without changing units, so 1.2 kg looks lighter than 950 g because 1.2 is a smaller number than 950. Change everything to grams first: 1.2 kg = 1200 g is actually the heaviest.

questions.prompt: Match each length to the same length in a different unit.
questions.solution: cm to mm: x 10, so 3.2 cm = 32 mm. m to cm: x 100, so 0.45 m = 45 cm and 1.08 m = 108 cm. km to m: x 1000, so 2.5 km = 2500 m.

misconceptions.common: Using the wrong number, for example x 100 for cm to mm (3.2 cm = 320 mm is wrong) or x 100 for km to m (2.5 km = 250 m is wrong). Remember: 10 mm = 1 cm, 100 cm = 1 m, 1000 m = 1 km.

questions.prompt: A jug holds 1.75 L of juice. Siti pours 4 cups of juice from the jug. Each cup holds 280 ml. How much juice is left in the jug?
questions.solution: Change litres to millilitres: 1.75 L = 1750 ml. Juice poured: 4 x 280 ml = 1120 ml. Juice left: 1750 - 1120 = 630 ml.

misconceptions.1: That is the juice Siti POURED OUT (4 x 280 ml). The question asks how much is LEFT, so subtract it from 1750 ml.
misconceptions.2: You took away only one cup (1.75 - 0.28 = 1.47). She pours 4 cups, so take away 4 x 280 ml = 1120 ml.
misconceptions.3: 0.63 is the right number of LITRES, but you wrote ml. 0.63 L = 630 ml. Always check the unit matches your number.

questions.prompt: Select ALL the masses that are equal to 2.05 kg.
questions.solution: 2.05 kg = 2.05 x 1000 g = 2050 g. That is 2 kg and 50 g. 2.050 kg is also the same, because a zero on the end of a decimal does not change its value. 2 kg 5 g = 2005 g and 205 g are different.

misconceptions.2: 2 kg 5 g = 2005 g. The 5 in 2.05 is in the hundredths place, so 0.05 kg = 50 g, not 5 g.
misconceptions.3: 205 g is what you get if you multiply by 100. There are 1000 g in 1 kg, so 2.05 kg = 2050 g.
misconceptions.common: Thinking 2.050 kg is different from 2.05 kg. Adding a zero at the END of a decimal does not change its value.

questions.prompt: Mei Lin has 2 bags of flour. Each bag holds 1.5 kg. Each cake needs 450 g of flour. She bakes as many whole cakes as she can. How much flour is left over? Give your answer in grams.
questions.solution: Total flour: 2 x 1.5 kg = 3 kg = 3000 g. Cakes: 450 g each. 6 x 450 = 2700 g and 7 x 450 = 3150 g, which is too much. So she bakes 6 cakes. Flour left: 3000 - 2700 = 300 g.

misconceptions.common: Using only one bag (1500 g) or forgetting to change kg to g. Change 3 kg to 3000 g first, then see how many 450 g lots fit.

questions.prompt: A rectangle is 8 cm long and 5 cm wide. What is its area? Give your answer in cm^2.
questions.solution: Area of a rectangle = length x width = 8 x 5 = 40 cm^2.

misconceptions.common: Adding the sides (8 + 5 + 8 + 5 = 26) gives the perimeter, not the area. Area means how many 1 cm squares cover the shape, so multiply.

questions.prompt: A rectangular garden is 12 m long and 7 m wide. What is its perimeter?
questions.solution: Perimeter is the distance all the way round. 12 + 7 + 12 + 7 = 38 m. Or 2 x (12 + 7) = 2 x 19 = 38 m.

misconceptions.0: You added only one length and one width. A rectangle has 4 sides, so double it: 2 x 19 = 38 m.
misconceptions.1: 12 x 7 = 84 is the AREA (in m^2). Perimeter is the distance around the edge, so add the four sides.
misconceptions.3: You added only three sides (12 + 12 + 7). Go all the way round: there are two widths as well as two lengths.

questions.prompt: A rectangle is 1.2 m long and 40 cm wide. What is its perimeter in centimetres?
questions.solution: First make the units the same: 1.2 m = 120 cm. Perimeter = 120 + 40 + 120 + 40 = 320 cm.

misconceptions.0: You added 1.2 and 40 without changing the units. 1.2 m is 120 cm, so change it first.
misconceptions.1: 120 + 40 = 160 is only one length and one width. Double it for all four sides: 320 cm.
misconceptions.2: 120 x 40 = 4800 is the area (in cm^2), not the perimeter. For perimeter, add the sides.

questions.prompt: A rug is 2.5 m long and 1.6 m wide. What is its area?
questions.solution: Area = length x width = 2.5 x 1.6. Work out 25 x 16 = 400. There are 2 decimal places in the question (one in each number), so the answer is 4.00 = 4 m^2.

misconceptions.1: 8.2 is the PERIMETER (2.5 + 1.6 + 2.5 + 1.6 = 8.2 m). Area needs length x width.
misconceptions.2: You added 2.5 + 1.6 = 4.1. For area you multiply length by width.
misconceptions.3: 25 x 16 = 400 is right, but you put the decimal point in the wrong place. 2.5 x 1.6 is about 2 x 2 = 4, so 4 m^2 makes sense.

questions.prompt: True or false: A rectangle 2 m long and 50 cm wide has an area of 100 m^2.
questions.solution: Make the units the same first. 50 cm = 0.5 m. Area = 2 x 0.5 = 1 m^2. So the statement is false. (2 x 50 = 100 mixes metres and centimetres.)

misconceptions.common: Multiplying 2 by 50 without changing the units. You must use the same unit for both sides before you multiply.

questions.prompt: A rectangular floor is 4.8 m long and 3.6 m wide. It is covered with square tiles, each 60 cm by 60 cm, with no gaps. How many tiles are needed?
questions.solution: Change to centimetres: 4.8 m = 480 cm and 3.6 m = 360 cm. Tiles along the length: 480 / 60 = 8. Tiles along the width: 360 / 60 = 6. Number of tiles = 8 x 6 = 48.

misconceptions.0: You found 8 tiles along the length and 6 along the width, but then added them. The tiles fill rows and columns, so multiply: 8 x 6 = 48.
misconceptions.1: You used the perimeter (16.8 m) and divided by 0.6 m. That counts tiles around the edge only. The floor is covered, so you need the area.
misconceptions.3: You worked out the area (17.28 m^2) and treated each tile as 1 m^2. Each tile is only 60 cm by 60 cm, which is much smaller than 1 m^2.

questions.prompt: A rectangle has an area of 54 cm^2. Its length is 9 cm. What is its perimeter?
questions.solution: Area = length x width, so width = 54 / 9 = 6 cm. Perimeter = 9 + 6 + 9 + 6 = 30 cm.

misconceptions.0: 9 + 6 = 15 is only one length and one width. A rectangle has two of each: 2 x 15 = 30 cm.
misconceptions.1: You found the width (6 cm) but then did 4 x 6, as if it were a square. The length is 9 cm, not 6 cm.
misconceptions.2: You used the area (54) as if it were a side length: 2 x (54 + 9). First find the width: 54 / 9 = 6 cm.

questions.prompt: A square has a perimeter of 3.2 m. What is its area? Give your answer in cm^2.
questions.solution: Change to centimetres: 3.2 m = 320 cm. A square has 4 equal sides, so each side = 320 / 4 = 80 cm. Area = 80 x 80 = 6400 cm^2.

misconceptions.common: Dividing the perimeter by 4 and stopping (80), or squaring the perimeter. Find the side first (320 / 4 = 80 cm), then multiply side x side.

questions.prompt: A rectangular playground is 25 m long and 18 m wide. Select ALL the statements that are true.
questions.solution: Perimeter = 25 + 18 + 25 + 18 = 86 m. In centimetres: 86 x 100 = 8600 cm, so that statement is also true. Area = 25 x 18 = 450 m^2. 43 is just 25 + 18, half the perimeter.

misconceptions.2: 43 = 25 + 18. Adding gives part of the perimeter, not the area. Area = 25 x 18 = 450 m^2.
misconceptions.4: 25 + 18 = 43 m is only one length and one width. The full perimeter is 2 x 43 = 86 m.
misconceptions.common: Missing that 8600 cm is the same as 86 m (1 m = 100 cm, so 86 m = 8600 cm).

questions.prompt: What is the name for the total distance around the edge of a shape?
questions.solution: The perimeter is the distance all the way around the edge of a shape. You find it by adding the lengths of all the sides.

misconceptions.common: Mixing up perimeter and area. Area is the space INSIDE a shape; perimeter is the distance AROUND it.

questions.prompt: Daniel wants to put a fence all the way around a rectangular field that is 15 m long and 9.5 m wide. Fencing costs RM 12 per metre. How much will the fencing cost?
questions.solution: The fence goes around the edge, so find the perimeter: 15 + 9.5 + 15 + 9.5 = 49 m. Cost = 49 x RM 12 = RM 588.

misconceptions.0: You used 15 + 9.5 = 24.5 m, which is only half the perimeter. The fence goes all the way round: 49 m.
misconceptions.2: You used the area (15 x 9.5 = 142.5 m^2). A fence goes around the edge, so you need the perimeter.
misconceptions.3: 49 m is the perimeter, but you stopped there. Each metre costs RM 12, so multiply: 49 x 12 = RM 588.

questions.prompt: Priya walks 1.2 km from home to school, then 850 m from school to the library. How far does she walk altogether, in metres?
questions.solution: Change to the same unit first: 1.2 km = 1.2 x 1000 = 1200 m. Then add: 1200 + 850 = 2050 m.

misconceptions.0: You added 1.2 and 850 without changing the units. 1.2 km is 1200 m, so change it first.
misconceptions.2: You changed 1.2 km to 120 m by multiplying by 100. There are 1000 m in a km, so 1.2 km = 1200 m.
misconceptions.3: 2.05 is the answer in KILOMETRES. The question asks for metres: 2.05 km = 2050 m.
